title: A missing/invalid API key on any eagerly-validating cloud provider (OpenAI, Groq, and by shared-class construction OpenRouter/xAI/DeepSeek) now surfaces the router's generic 'The terminal hit an internal error... restart Vysted' frame instead of a humanized 'add your API key in Settings' message, on both /agents/{id}/invoke and /llm/chat
repro: python3 scripts/r15/vy.py invoke copilot "hi" --port 52320 --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --mode agent --autonomy ask --no-key -> SSE {"kind":"error","message":"The terminal hit an internal error.","action":"Try again; if it keeps happening, restart Vysted.","detail":"OpenAIError: Missing credentials...","code":"internal"}. Reproduced identically for provider=groq (GroqError: api_key client option must be set...) and via a direct curl to /llm/chat for provider=openai. Provider=anthropic on the SAME /llm/chat route correctly humanizes to {message:'Something went wrong with Anthropic.', action:'Try again or switch provider in Settings.', code:'unknown'} because Anthropic's SDK defers key validation to request time, while OpenAI's/Groq's SDK client constructor raises immediately.
suspected_files: sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:591 (client = self._client(api_key) called before the try: at :651, so a client-construction OpenAIError never reaches this adapter's own try/except or humanize())
sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py, sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py (same shape but their SDKs do not raise eagerly, so they are not currently exposed by this gap)
sidecar/routers/agents.py:106-110 (except Exception: yield error_frame(exc) unconditionally, never tries humanize(provider_id, exc) first)

sidecar/services/errors.py:552-568 (error_frame() is hardcoded generic 'internal' by design per R15-AGENT-030's fix_shape, on the premise that 'adapters already humanize their own failures' before reaching the router guard — that premise is false for this call path)

title: Citation-integrity net still only recognises a bare '[n]' marker; a model-written non-numeric bracket token (e.g. a literal internal scheme URL) ships unprocessed in the published brief
repro: Gate round 3, candidate 01d6920a300b016ab1ad8aa436ee4e4586f8e336, own sidecar 127.0.0.1:52321 (data dir rc1-round-3-data-rc1-drive-research-briefs, fresh copy of rc1-round-3-seed-data). `python3 scripts/r15/vy.py invoke copilot 'Do a deep research brief on CG Power and Industrial Solutions — order book, margins, and whether the valuation is justified versus peers.' --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --autonomy auto --options '{"research_depth":"deep"}' --port 52321` -> published brief markdown (docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/rc1/round-3/1-deep-cgpower-llama.jsonl, publish_brief tool_use) contains SIX literal instances of the token `[vysted://fundamentals/CGPOWER]` in the '### Order Book and Valuation' and '### Financial Performance' sections (e.g. 'Price to Book Ratio: 17.51 [vysted://fundamentals/CGPOWER]', 'Revenue Growth (QoQ): +14.0% [vysted://fundamentals/CGPOWER]') — the model wrote the source's internal scheme URL directly inside brackets instead of its correct numeric marker (the brief's own sources array maps index 7 to that exact URL, so '[7]' was available and correct). Direct repro: `python3 -c "import re; MARKER_RE = re.compile(r'\[(\d{1,3})\](?!\()'); print(MARKER_RE.findall('[vysted://fundamentals/CGPOWER]'))"` -> `[]` (no match) against BOTH sidecar/services/research/citecheck.py's MARKER_RE and src/lib/brief-ingest.ts's identical CITE_MARKER_RE (`/\[(\d{1,3})\](?!\()/g`). Because the pattern requires the bracket to contain ONLY 1-3 digits, the token is never evaluated as in-range or out-of-range by strip_invalid_markers, never matched by strip_model_bibliography's literal-'[n]' cleanup, and never turned into a resolvable citation chip by the frontend — it ships through verbatim as dead bracket text exposing an internal URL scheme to the end user. Not reproduced in the same session's BDL DEEP (gpt-4o-mini, with context) or Kaynes ULTRA (gpt-4o-mini) runs — zero non-numeric bracket tokens in either — so the trigger is model-quality-dependent (the weaker local model), but the regex gap itself is unconditional and any lane/model can ship the same failure shape. This is the same underlying defect class independently found in gate round 2's un-register-tracked finding (a bracket holding '[New findings]' or a multi-number group '[2, 3]') — that finding is NOT cited as this round's evidence per the harness rule (round 2 is a different gate round), but the class recurs here in a third distinct shape (a scheme URL) on an independently-driven candidate, confirming the regex is the root cause rather than any one bad output.

title: Proposed-change review card and applied label price a US lot in the session region's currency (Add 4 MSFT @ ₹480 for a $480 lot)
repro: Region IN (seed profile). Copilot on llama3.1:8b, --autonomy ask: 'I bought 4 shares of MSFT at 480 dollars per share. Add that position to my tracked portfolio with portfolio_add_position.' -> tool_use portfolio_add_position {MSFT, 4, 480}; frontend enqueue -> review card title 'Add 4 MSFT @ ₹480 to the portfolio', after 'Portfolio: +MSFT ×4 @ ₹480 (3 total)'. Same for the order-attempt write: 'Add 10 AAPL @ ₹0'. The ledger stores 480 correctly and the Portfolio panel renders it with the quote currency ($), so only the text the user accepts is wrong (contradicts D57).
